findings.decompiled: mem[ceil32(_1) + ceil32(_2) + ... + ceil32(_12) + 160 len 4] = 157198259 / while idx < 68: mem[idx + ceil32(_1) + ... + 228] = ...; idx = idx + 32 / call fundsAsset with: args mem[ceil32(_1) + ... + 228 len ...]
findings.issue: The encoded call is copied into the call buffer by a word loop (even with the constant length 68), so approve/transfer calls show raw memory; the buffer addresses are printed as sums of ten ceil32 terms (the free pointer after ten calls), which makes these lines several hundred characters long.
findings.rule: Turn 'while i < n: mem[d + i] = mem[s + i]; i += 32' into a copy line (same rule as c00548), then decode the call; name the free-memory pointer value when it is stored (mem[64] = E) and express later addresses as that name plus a constant.

notes: No explicit loop in the source of the 28 ABI functions or what they reach (open-term LoanManager, ERC20Helper, MapleProxied). The 15 whiles are implicit: bytes[] calldata encodings for acceptNewTerms/rejectNewTerms-style calls (37fdb36f, dac83f8d) and ERC20Helper payload copies (P7). Reviewed in detail: fund, triggerDefault, the claim path and the getters; no semantic error found. Packed slots are read through shifts (P15).
summary: Faithful and loop-free in the source; ERC20Helper calls lose their decoded form because the payload copy stays a word loop, and buffer addresses grow into long sums of ceil32 terms.
